The event's entry from the loader: turns off the CIA's interrupts, clears $10 to $8F, points the ripple pointer at $8800, banks out the ROMs, installs the raster interrupt at $958E, sets up the screen and the sprites, and goes to the main loop.
Calls two routines that only return.
Sets up the screen, the background colour and the sprites.

Runs one race: sets up the screen, the pacer's skill ($58) and the start positions, places both boats, waits for both fire buttons up, plays the tune, waits for the players at the start, says READY SET GO, then rows until both boats have finished and stopped. Waits for a fire button before returning.
The pacer's skill starts at $58, about one stroke in three wrong.
Steps the start positions 16 times: boat 0 ends at $137 and boat 1 at $12B, each $179D short of its finish.
No time flashes yet; draws both lanes once.
Silences the SID.
Waits until no fire button has been pressed for 100 checks.
Plays the tune, waits for the players, stops it, and counts down.
Zeroes the clock, the times, the finish flags, the speeds and the meters.
Each frame draws the top lane then the bottom one; works out which time to flash (1 for the top, 2 for the bottom, 0 while they are the same); and loops until both boats have finished and stopped.
Clears the speeds and the meters, plays the tune and waits for a fire button.
Back to the main loop.

The raster line each lane waits for before it draws its water row, so the row is drawn after the beam has passed it: $96 for the top lane, $13 for the bottom one.

Slot 0, line $F1: at the bottom of the screen turns the fine scroll off, plays the tune or steps the sound effects, moves the waves on, counts down the ripples, reads F3 and F5, and flashes the winner's time.
Moves the waves on: a quarter step each frame, through 20 steps.
Counts down eight ripple timers each frame, so each timer is counted every 128 frames.
Reads keyboard row 0: F5 sets key_flag and F3 clears it.
Flashes the faster boat's time on its status line, white and yellow every 16 frames.
The colours of the flashing time: white, then yellow.
Counts down each frame; bit 4 picks the colour.
Which time flashes: 0 none, 1 the top lane's, 2 the bottom lane's.

Sets up the screen: video bank $4000, the screen at $4000; fills it with the course's first character in colour 9; row 0 with character $58; rows 11 and 23 with the course's second character; and rows 12 and 24 with the status lines, white.
Two RTS bytes nothing reaches.

Draws the top lane's water row (row 6) from the course at lane_ptr: each column whose ripple timer runs and whose wave kind is set takes that kind's wave character for the step of the waves, the others the course's own character. Then starts a ripple 15 columns in, where the boat is.

Draws one lane, X: points lane_ptr at the course for its boat's position, waits for the lane's raster line, sets its fine scroll and draws its water row. Then places each boat in the other's lane by the gap between them, reads the strokes, and after the bottom lane moves the boats on.
For each boat, works out the gap to the other one.
Writes the gap into each sprite's X, starting from boat_layout; a sprite more than a screen away goes off the right edge at $1D0.

The same table's high byte, for a sprite sent off the screen.
Reads the lane's stroke and sounds its oars.
After the bottom lane: notes the times, sets the sprite frames and the meters, checks the finish, and moves both boats on by their speeds.
Checks both boats against the finish.

Boat X's stroke each frame: works out its speed index (0 to 15) from its speed. Every fourth frame reads its stick (or the pacer's choice) and steps its stroke phase: on with the stick right, on through the stroke with it left, or back to rest with neither, from three tables.
A boat that has finished drifts back to rest.

Reads the boat's joystick: the port the player chose at the start.
Neither way: the phase from stroke_none.
Right: the phase from stroke_right.
Left: the phase from stroke_left.

The speed lost each frame at each speed index, more the faster the boat goes.
How fast the stick is read at each speed index: $40, every fourth frame at every speed.

Whether each boat's oars were in the water last frame.
When the oars are in the water: after 8 frames there each frame adds the gain to the speed. Then takes the drag off, stopping at zero.
Redraws boat X's speed meter while it moves: the length is its speed times 4, at most 16 bars.

The pacer's stroke: adjusts its skill, then takes a random number; below the skill it plays the right stick, otherwise 0, which reads as right.
The pacer's skill: up by one while it is behind the player, to $FF; while ahead, down by one (by two above $90) but not below $58.
The name COMPUTER PACER.

The main loop. In practice player 1 rows against COMPUTER PACER and the event returns to the menu. In competition the players row in pairs, the next player in the top lane, or each against the pacer when there is one joystick or the number is odd. Each time goes into the player's record as its score, inverted so a lower time is a higher score, and the status line's text is copied into the record.
Competition.
Puts the next player's name in the top lane and this one's in the bottom lane.
Against the pacer.
Races, then stores the bottom player's time.
And the top player's, unless the pacer rowed it.
Copies the time's text from the status lines.
The next player, or the next pair.

Waits for the fire buttons up, then flashes PRESS YOUR BUTTON for the bottom lane until a button is pressed; that port is the bottom boat's. Then the same for the top lane and the other button, unless the pacer rows.
The starter's gun: noise on voice 3.

Starts the event's tune and turns the music on.

The music driver, called each frame: for a new tune reads which voices it uses and starts each at its notes. Then for each voice, when its note's time is up, reads the voice's next bytes: $FF ends it, $FE lo hi jumps, $FD n sets the length of the notes, a byte below $80 is a note (an index into the frequency table, $7F a rest) followed by how many times the set length it lasts, and $FC is followed by pairs of a SID register and its value, until a byte of $80 or more.
Two bytes inside music_step that nothing reads.
Each voice in turn, from the third: counts down its note, repeats the length as often as the note asked, then reads its next bytes.
Two bytes after music_step that nothing reads.
Points voice Y at its notes from the tune's header.
Moves the music pointer on and reads the byte there.
Clears the gate bit of voice X, ending its note.
Code nothing calls, from a version of the music driver: works out a SID register from a voice.
The offset of each voice's variables and SID registers: 0, 7 and 14.
The SID frequency of each note, low byte then high byte.
The table read one byte on, for the high bytes of the frequencies.
The last byte of the frequency table.
